## Software tools to install

Everything is free. Install in roughly this order; the large downloads (R, Python, VS Code, Positron, TinyTeX) can run in the background while you work through the rest. Step-by-step instructions, a verification checkpoint, and a troubleshooting table are in the course book: [Chapter 1](book/chapters/01-introduction.html#sec-intro-setup) (operating-system setup) and [Chapter 2](book/chapters/02-your-toolkit.html) (everything else).

-   **VS Code** and **Positron** (editors/IDEs)
-   A **Unix shell** (built in on Mac and Linux; WSL with Ubuntu on Windows) that can `ssh` to the UO computing cluster (Talapas)
-   Latest version of **R**
-   **Python 3**
-   **Quarto**, plus **TinyTeX** (a small LaTeX) for PDF output
-   **Git** and a **GitHub** account for version control and collaboration

Your laptop needs 16 GB of RAM (8 GB minimum), about 20 GB of free disk space, an up-to-date macOS, Windows 10/11, or Linux, and administrator rights. Chromebooks and iPads will not work.

## Editors and IDEs

-   [VS Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/download), with the Quarto, Python, R, and Jupyter extensions (and WSL on Windows)
-   [Positron](https://positron.posit.co/download), Posit's data-science IDE; install R and Python first so it can find them

## Terminal applications

### *Mac users*

-   Open the native **Terminal** app (`Cmd-Space`, type "Terminal"), or install another terminal like [iTerm2](https://iterm2.com)
-   Install Apple's command-line developer tools (compilers and Git): in Terminal, run `xcode-select --install` and click **Install**
-   Optional: [Homebrew](https://brew.sh), a package manager for command-line software

### *Linux users*

-   Open your distribution's terminal app (often `Ctrl-Alt-T`)
-   Install the compiler toolchain: `sudo apt install build-essential gfortran` (Ubuntu/Debian)

### *Windows users*

-   Guide: <https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/wsl/install>
-   Run Windows PowerShell as administrator
-   Install WSL2 *and* Ubuntu by typing `wsl --install` (this does both; if Ubuntu does not appear afterwards, `wsl --install -d Ubuntu`)
-   Restart your computer
-   If it fails: run Windows Update, enable virtualization in the BIOS/UEFI, then `wsl --update` and try again

### *Accessing the shell on Windows*

-   Open **Ubuntu** from the Start menu and set up a username and password
-   These do not have to match your login info for Windows; nothing appears while you type the password, which is normal
-   Note that this is the Ubuntu Linux system you just installed, not Windows PowerShell
-   Run `sudo apt update` then `sudo apt upgrade` to ensure everything is up to date
-   Then install the compiler toolchain: `sudo apt install build-essential gfortran`
-   Keep your course folders and files inside your Ubuntu home directory (`~`); your Windows files are reachable from Ubuntu at `/mnt/c/Users/<name>`
-   Install R, Python, VS Code, and Positron as ordinary **Windows** programs, not inside Ubuntu

## Scripting languages

### R

-   Latest version of R ([install here](https://cran.r-project.org)); on a Mac pick the installer matching your chip (Apple menu → About This Mac: **arm64** for Apple silicon, **x86_64** for Intel); on Windows choose "base"; on Ubuntu `sudo apt install r-base r-base-dev`
-   Windows only: [Rtools](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/) matching your R version, so packages can be compiled
-   Once R is installed, in the R console: `install.packages("tidyverse")`

### Python

-   Python 3 from [python.org](https://www.python.org/downloads/); on Windows, check **"Add python.exe to PATH"** on the first installer screen
-   Alternatives: [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) or Miniconda/Miniforge; any one is fine, just pick one
-   On Ubuntu/WSL: `sudo apt install python3-pip python3-venv`

## Quarto and LaTeX

-   Latest version of Quarto ([install here](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/))
-   Then, in a terminal: `quarto install tinytex` (a small LaTeX distribution; or `tinytex::install_tinytex()` from R)
-   A full LaTeX distribution ([MacTeX](https://www.tug.org/mactex/), [MiKTeX](https://miktex.org/download), or TeX Live) works too if you already have one
-   Check with `quarto check`

## Git and GitHub

-   Latest version of Git ([install here](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Getting-Started-Installing-Git)); on a Mac it comes with the Xcode command-line tools, on Ubuntu `sudo apt install git`
-   A GitHub account ([sign up here](https://github.com/signup)) using your UO email so you qualify for the [Student Developer Pack](https://education.github.com/pack)

## Check that it all works

Open a terminal (or the terminal inside VS Code or Positron) and run:

```bash
echo $SHELL
R --version
python3 --version
quarto --version
quarto check
git --version
```

Each should print a version, not "command not found". If one is missing, close and reopen the terminal first (it only sees programs installed before it started), then see the [troubleshooting table](book/chapters/02-your-toolkit.html#sec-toolkit-checkpoint) in the book.
